Methodology and coverage +

We searched combinations of week numbers, season parity, score digits, ESPN’s home/away labels, previous-week results, and opponents. Each featured record matches at least five games across at least two seasons. We deliberately selected unusually one-sided results from many possible combinations. These are mined coincidences, not evidence that the conditions cause wins.

Coverage includes completed regular-season and championship-bracket matchups from 2019–2025. Consolation games, byes, the ongoing 2026 season, and the unavailable 2018 archive are excluded. Ownerless team #12 is excluded from 2022 onward; it was a real team in 2019–2021. No league-average matchup is treated as a scored game in this page’s records.

Records follow ESPN team slots across renamed teams and possible ownership changes. Cards use current team labels where available; receipts retain the names from each season. “Home” and “away” are ESPN matchup labels, not real stadiums. “Prime” means a number greater than one divisible only by itself and one. A score’s whole-number part drops its decimal places.

“The week after” requires an included matchup in the immediately preceding week of the same season. Scores are compared as integer hundredths. Ties are retained in records; overall records refer to the same included archive. Every claim lists all matching games and links to the ESPN scoreboard. No player-level, weather, or day-of-week claims are inferred from team scores.
